purpose: Screenshot-based visual design mockups; no live application changes

prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE polished, realistic tablet UI design mockup by redesigning the supplied actual FactoryLM Hub screenshot. Reference image is today's real interface: retain the FactoryLM wordmark, its navy header, white sidebar, pale cool-gray content, purple primary actions, sans-serif typography and rounded controls. This is a proposed product design, NOT a photograph or presentation slide.
Output: one straight-on, full-frame landscape tablet app screen, 2304x1440 if possible, aspect 8:5. Remove browser address bar, OS chrome, account email and unrelated project names. App fills the canvas; no device bezel, no perspective, no decorative background. Crisp legible text, strong contrast, large touch targets, restrained spacing. Footer in small clear text: "Proposed design — simulated state".
SCREEN 1: HOME — FIND EQUIPMENT AND RESUME.
Left sidebar about 250 px: FactoryLM wordmark, Home selected, Equipment, Conversations, collapsed Projects. A purple "Ask a question" button. No invented tenant or customer names, no giant project/chat tree.
Navy top bar across the main area: "Home" on left. Main content header "Where are you working?" with supporting text "Find equipment or pick up where you left off." Search field "Find equipment by name, tag or location".
Section "Recent equipment": one generous simple equipment card "Conveyor 1", secondary "Home Garage / Conveyor Lab", understated line "Drive and MLC bench pilot", outlined "Open equipment" button with arrow. Small diagram-like equipment icon, not a fake photo. No green operational badges, no live readings, no device-status claims, no completion percentages.
Section "Recent conversations": two clean rows; "Check MLC identification" with secondary "Conveyor 1 · MLC · Identity not confirmed", action "Resume"; "Review drive manual" with secondary "Conveyor 1 · VFD1", action "Resume". Both are labelled conversations, not jobs.
Lower compact card: "Just have a document?" "Ask a question without selecting equipment." action "Ask a question".
The hierarchy must make finding the machine and resuming a specific conversation immediately obvious. Preserve the familiar visual language of the real screenshot but remove overlapping floating buttons and clutter. No dashboard charts, 19-row inventory, industrial control commands, new workflow engine, generic marketing copy or robot illustration.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE polished high-fidelity landscape tablet screen, straight-on, full app canvas, 2304x1440 if possible, 8:5 aspect. Image 1 is the approved HOME mockup: match its FactoryLM wordmark, navy header, white sidebar, pale cool-gray body, purple buttons, typography, spacing and proportions exactly as a screen from the same app. Image 2 is today's actual Hub components screenshot, reference for real product concepts and unconfirmed identity state. Redesign the current interface; no device bezel, OS/browser chrome, private email, unrelated projects, perspective, marketing illustrations or charts. Crisp large readable text and large touch targets; no controls floating over content. Sidebar remains FactoryLM; Home, Equipment (selected), Conversations, collapsed Projects; bottom "Ask a question". Footer exactly "Proposed design — simulated state". This is a proposal, not proof of verified equipment or real saved work.
SCREEN 2 — CONVEYOR 1 EQUIPMENT WORKSPACE.
Navy header "Conveyor 1". Main heading "Conveyor 1"; secondary "Home Garage / Conveyor Lab". A quiet gray status beside the title "Current condition: Unknown". A top toolbar primary "Ask about Conveyor 1", secondary "Open work record". Below a simple tab row "Overview" selected, "Conversations", "Manuals", "Work record".
Main section "Components" with exactly TWO well-spaced rows/cards. First: "VFD1" bold, secondary "Drive", button "Open component". Second: "MLC" bold, secondary "Installed role not verified", amber badge "Identity not confirmed", button "Check label", secondary action "Open component". No claim that MLC is a verified contactor or matching control relay.
Below two balanced panels: left "Manuals and prints" with one document row "CA3KN22BD-maker.pdf", secondary "Catalog reference · applicability not confirmed", action "Open source". Right "Recent conversation" row "Check MLC identification", subtitle "MLC · Conversation", action "Resume".
Bottom compact full-width work area "Work record" with secondary "Jobs, notes and photos for this equipment", action "Open work record". Do not invent a new job lifecycle, machine availability signal, completed task, verification checkmark or live value. Components must be first-class objects inside one named machine, not separate projects.

Image 1 is the approved HOME mockup: match its FactoryLM wordmark, navy header, white sidebar, pale cool-gray body, purple buttons, typography, spacing and proportions exactly as a screen from the same app. Image 2 is today's actual Hub components screenshot, reference for real product concepts and unconfirmed identity state. Redesign the current interface; no device bezel, OS/browser chrome, private email, unrelated projects, perspective, marketing illustrations or charts. Crisp large readable text and large touch targets; no controls floating over content. Sidebar remains FactoryLM; Home, Equipment (selected), Conversations, collapsed Projects; bottom "Ask a question". Footer exactly "Proposed design — simulated state". This is a proposal, not proof of verified equipment or real saved work.
SCREEN 3 — MLC CONVERSATION AND DOCUMENT EVIDENCE.
Navy header "Conveyor 1 / MLC" with small "Back to equipment" action. Main area split into a broad conversation pane and a narrower source pane, separated by a clean divider. Source pane occupies about 35% of main width. It must never cover the conversation or composer.
Conversation title "Check MLC identification". User message "What is the coil voltage of the selected MLC?" MIRA response in plain readable text: "MLC's identity has not been confirmed. Check its label before using this manual for the installed component." Below response clear outlined "Check label" button, amber small badge "Identity not confirmed". No installed-equipment electrical answer and no green verification badges.
Right pane header "Source" with close icon. Filename "CA3KN22BD-maker.pdf", "Page 1 of 4". Show a clean legible catalog-reference excerpt card, not an invented photographed datasheet: "CA3KN22BD", "TeSys K control relay", a small 2-row table "Control voltage   24 V DC" and "Contacts   2 NO + 2 NC". Below: "Document data only" and "Installed MLC not verified." Link "Open full page". The referenced document does support those catalog facts, but its applicability to the installed MLC is unconfirmed.
Anchor the context strip immediately ABOVE the composer inside the conversation pane, in its own space: label "About: Conveyor 1 → MLC", small "Change" button; second line amber "Identity not confirmed". Composer with Attach icon, placeholder "Ask about MLC…", high-contrast "Send" button. Current target is always obvious; context is separate from source facts. Do not use a floating Whole machine chip, prepare job overlay or fake current telemetry.

Image 1 is the approved HOME mockup: match its FactoryLM wordmark, navy header, white sidebar, pale cool-gray body, purple buttons, typography, spacing and proportions exactly as a screen from the same app. Image 2 is today's actual Hub components screenshot, reference for real product concepts and unconfirmed identity state. Redesign the current interface; no device bezel, OS/browser chrome, private email, unrelated projects, perspective, marketing illustrations or charts. SCREEN 4 — RECOVER WHEN ANOTHER SCREEN CHANGES THE SELECTED COMPONENT.
Same overall app and sidebar. Navy header "Conveyor 1". Title "Check MLC identification". Conversation area intentionally modest with one previous MIRA entry "MLC's identity has not been confirmed." Leave enough room to fit recovery and the entire draft above a realistic tablet software keyboard.
Near the bottom of the app, an inline amber-bordered recovery card in dedicated flow, NEVER a popover. Heading "Selection changed on another screen". Text "Your question has not been sent." Two explicit comparison rows: "Previous: Conveyor 1 → MLC" and "Current: Conveyor 1 · No component selected". Two distinct legible buttons on one row: purple "Return to MLC" and outlined "Review for current selection". Small plain instruction "Review the target, then send your question." Do not auto-send or silently rewrite the draft.
Immediately below this card and above the keyboard, show the retained draft in the composer exactly "What is the coil voltage of the selected component?" Attach icon at left. Send button visibly disabled until a target decision, with legible label "Send". Current-target strip above draft says "About: Conveyor 1 · No component selected". All warning text and both recovery actions must be visible while the keyboard is open.
Bottom approximately 24% of canvas: a quiet realistic light-gray Android landscape keyboard, ordinary QWERTY rows, not a focus of the design. Integrate the footer "Proposed design — simulated state" unobtrusively at top-right of content if bottom is occupied. No source proof, wrong-scope answer, vague network error, offscreen Retry, or disappearing text.

Use case: ui-mockup / comparison board.
Create one clean high-resolution landscape design review board, 3200x2000 if possible, from the FIVE supplied reference images. This is a layout/compositing task. Image 1 is the actual FactoryLM Hub tablet screenshot captured today. Images 2, 3, 4 and 5 are proposed mockups already approved as this visual set. Preserve the UI appearance and text of the supplied screens as closely as possible, do not design different screens.
Board title "FactoryLM Hub — proposed tablet experience". Subtitle "Today's interface → equipment, context, evidence and recovery".
White/light cool gray board, dark navy typography, very restrained purple accent. No marketing ornament, no fake devices or perspective, no dense annotations.
Layout: narrow LEFT column about 30% width showing the actual screenshot with label "TODAY · ACTUAL SCREENSHOT". Crop away browser/OS chrome and the bottom account-email area; crop or obscure unrelated project titles so no private account information or unrelated project data is reproduced. Keep the actual current title, chat, large project list structure, floating Whole machine / Prepare job / Job sheet controls and bottom composer recognizable. Do not invent new current-state content or improve the actual screen. Under it, two concise observation captions "Equipment is buried in projects" and "Floating controls obscure content".
RIGHT area about 66% width, 2 by 2 grid of the four proposed mockups, in this exact sequence: image 2 upper-left, image 3 upper-right, image 4 lower-left, image 5 lower-right. Give each a clean number and caption OUTSIDE its screen: "1  Find equipment & resume", "2  Open the machine", "3  Check context & evidence", "4  Recover without losing work". Preserve their readable larger headings and major controls. No new diagrams or altered semantics. It is fine for tiny UI text to be too small at board scale; the individual full-size screens are the authoritative details.
Below the right grid, one small line "Drive + MLC only · Existing projects remain accessible".
Footer across board exactly "Proposed design — simulated state. Visual mockups, not a deployed interface or field-verification result."
Use the source images directly as reference for composition. The board must clearly distinguish the actual screenshot from the proposed screens. Do not turn the unconfirmed MLC into confirmed equipment, do not claim machine running, no green success badges.

Edit this comparison board with one strictly targeted text correction, preserving ALL layout, thumbnails, colors and other text unchanged. The left panel is a reconstruction derived from the real screenshot, not the original screenshot pixels, so replace its heading "TODAY · ACTUAL SCREENSHOT" with "TODAY · SCREENSHOT-BASED REFERENCE". Fit it on two lines if needed at readable size within the existing heading space. Also replace the very bottom footer with "Left: recreated from today's screenshot. Right: proposed designs with simulated state." Do not alter the four proposed mockups or redraw the other UI. Keep the large title and all other captions unchanged. No privacy details may be added.
